comment: Counterexample catalog for window aggregation. Every expectation is hand-computed and expressed as a rational literal; no value here was produced by running window.Aggregate or window.Bucket. Each plausible_wrong entry encodes a concrete buggy rule whose output looks reasonable; the test fails if the implementation matches any of them. See docs/window-testing.md for the derivation of every number.

cases.name: negative-delta-floor-attribution
cases.comment: t=-4 with origin=7 step=10: delta=-11, floor division gives window [-13,-3). Truncated division toward zero puts the point in [-3,7), a window that starts after the point.

cases.name: upper-edge-belongs-to-next-window
cases.comment: Windows are half-open: t=10 and t=20 are the first points of [10,20) and [20,30), never members of the window they close.

plausible_wrong.rule: boundary point assigned to the window it closes (closed upper edge)

cases.name: origin-shifts-the-lattice
cases.comment: origin=-3 step=7: windows start at ...,-10,-3,4,11,... Ignoring the origin and aligning to the Unix epoch produces tidy-looking but wrong windows.

plausible_wrong.rule: origin ignored, windows aligned to the Unix epoch

cases.name: average-weights-observations-not-series
cases.comment: Series id-a contributes 3 observations, id-b contributes 1. The average weights observations: (1+2+3+10)/4 = 4. Averaging per-series averages gives 6, which silently overweights the sparse series.

cases.name: first-tie-broken-by-smaller-series-id
cases.comment: Both series have their oldest point at t=50. The tie is broken by series ID: id-a < id-b, so first is id-a's value 5. The series list deliberately puts id-b first to tempt arrival-order tie-breaking.

plausible_wrong.rule: first tie broken by arrival order (id-b arrived first)

cases.name: last-tie-broken-by-larger-series-id
cases.comment: Both series have their newest point at t=80. The tie is broken by series ID: id-b > id-a, so last is id-b's value 3.

plausible_wrong.rule: last tie broken by arrival order (id-a arrived last)

cases.name: rate-reset-counts-as-zero-plus-restart
cases.comment: Counter 0,10,3,8: the drop 10->3 is a reset to zero, so increase is 10+3+5=18 over 3s = 6/s. Taking last-first loses the reset; dropping the negative delta loses the restart value 3.

plausible_wrong.rule: negative delta clamped to zero without crediting the restart value

cases.name: rate-denominator-is-observed-elapsed
cases.comment: Two points 1s apart inside a 10s window: the denominator is the observed elapsed time (1s), not the window width (10s).

plausible_wrong.rule: window width used as the rate denominator

cases.name: rate-single-point-windows-emit-nothing
cases.comment: Each window observes the counter only once: no elapsed time exists, so no rate cell may appear. Only populated, at-least-two-observation windows produce rates.

cases.name: decimal-tenths-sum-needs-rational-tolerance
cases.comment: 0.1+0.1+0.1 is 0.30000000000000004 in binary64, one ulp above 3/10. The expectation 3/10 is exact as a rational and matched with tolerance; demanding exact equality with decimal 0.3 is a test-authoring bug, not an implementation bug.

plausible_wrong.rule: golden value compared with exact decimal equality (test bug)

cases.name: group-key-omits-absent-labels
cases.comment: Series id-b has no zone label. Its group key is the empty set {}, not {zone:""}: label absence is preserved, matching the series-identity contract.

plausible_wrong.rule: absent label materialized as the empty string in the group key

cases.name: min-seeded-from-first-value-not-zero
cases.comment: All values are negative. The minimum is -5; an accumulator seeded at 0 instead of the first observation returns a phantom 0 that was never measured.

cases.name: max-seeded-from-first-value-not-zero
cases.comment: All values are negative. The maximum is -2; an accumulator seeded at 0 returns a phantom 0.
